The Design of Everyday R Functions

Jon Harmon, Atorus Research

“All artificial things are designed.”

1️⃣ Make functionality obvious

2️⃣ Forgive “close enough” input

3️⃣ Help users fix mistakes

  • Point out link to slides.
  • “This is obviously true for doors and teapots, but it’s also true for functions, even if the ‘design’ is the prompt you gave to AI.”

Make functionality obvious

Which dial controls which burner?

What does this function do?

my_fun <- function(x, y, z) {
  y2 <- ceiling(y * z * 100) / 100
  y3 <- y + y2
  data.frame(
    item = x,
    price = y,
    sales_tax = y2,
    total_price = y3
  )
}

Make it obvious what functions do

compile_sales_df <- function(x, y, z) {
  y2 <- ceiling(y * z * 100) / 100
  y3 <- y + y2
  data.frame(
    item = x,
    price = y,
    sales_tax = y2,
    total_price = y3
  )
}

Forgive “close enough” input

Which way do these batteries go?

non-directional battery

What happens if data types are incorrect?

compile_sales_df(
  items = c("paper towels", "toilet paper"),
  prices = c(12.33, 20.77)
)

What happens if data types are incorrect?

compile_sales_df(
  items = c("paper towels", "toilet paper"),
  prices = c(12.33, 20.77)

compile_sales_df <- function(items, prices, tax_rate = 0.0825) {
  prices <- stbl::to_dbl(prices)
  tax_rate <- stbl::to_dbl_scalar(tax_rate)
  items <- stbl::to_chr(items)
  sales_tax <- ceiling(prices * tax_rate * 100) / 100
  total_price <- prices + sales_tax
  data.frame(
    item = items,
    price = prices,
    sales_tax = sales_tax,
    total_price = total_price
  )
}

Help users fix mistakes

Why did I make this package?

compile_sales_df <- function(items, prices, tax_rate = 0.0825) {
  prices <- stbl::to_dbl(prices)
  tax_rate <- stbl::to_dbl_scalar(tax_rate)
  items <- stbl::to_chr(items)
  sales_tax <- ceiling(prices * tax_rate * 100) / 100
  total_price <- prices + sales_tax
  data.frame(
    item = items,
    price = prices,
    sales_tax = sales_tax,
    total_price = total_price
  )
}

Why did I make this package?

compile_sales_df <- function(items, prices, tax_rate = 0.0825) {
  prices <- as.double(prices)
  tax_rate <- as.double(tax_rate)
  items <- as.character(items)
  sales_tax <- ceiling(prices * tax_rate * 100) / 100
  total_price <- prices + sales_tax
  data.frame(
    item = items,
    price = prices,
    sales_tax = sales_tax,
    total_price = total_price
  )
}

Help users fix mistakes

compile_sales_df <- function(items, prices, tax_rate = 0.0825) {
  prices <- stbl::to_dbl(prices) |>
    stbl::replace_stbl_error(
      c(
        "{.arg prices} must be numeric",
        i = "Check that the input CSV is formatted correctly"
      )
    )
  sales_tax <- ceiling(prices * tax_rate * 100) / 100
  total_price <- prices + sales_tax
  data.frame(
    item = items,
    price = prices,
    sales_tax = sales_tax,
    total_price = total_price
  )
}

Help users fix mistakes

compile_sales_df <- function(items, prices, tax_rate = 0.0825) {
  prices <- stbl::to_dbl(prices) |>
    stbl::replace_stbl_error(
      c(
        "{.arg prices} must be numeric",
        i = "Check that the input CSV is formatted correctly"
      ),
      subclass = c("incompatible_values", "double")
    )
  sales_tax <- ceiling(prices * tax_rate * 100) / 100
  total_price <- prices + sales_tax
  data.frame(
    item = items,
    price = prices,
    sales_tax = sales_tax,
    total_price = total_price
  )
}
